_decision: Origin ships Inter. Our --font-sans is already Inter-first with system fallbacks, so nothing had to change — an exact match rather than a divergence.
_scale: Values come from the approved type mapping, not from measuring the component: Tailwind's own theme.css defines --text-base 1rem/1.5rem, --text-sm 0.875rem/1.25rem, --text-xs 0.75rem/1rem, --font-weight-medium 500.
_scope: Asserted on the panel title because the family is inherited and any real text element proves it. The FIRST family in the stack is what matters — a fallback firing would mean the font failed to load, which is a different failure from the wrong family being configured.
_value_source: The expected stack is read from tokens/base.tokens.json's own font-sans $value at spec-authoring time and joined, NOT copied from the browser. That direction matters: a token change must fail this check, and an expectation pasted from a measurement can never fail — it would only ever re-describe whatever the component currently does.
_why_the_whole_stack: The first attempt asserted just "Inter" and failed, because getComputedStyle returns the resolved stack. Asserting the whole stack is the stronger claim anyway: it proves Inter is FIRST and that the fallbacks are the intended ones. A stack that silently lost its system fallbacks would pass an Inter-only check.
